xmldoc.short_description: Turn an FMU into a native nflow block manifest.

param_input_item.param_description: a string scalar or character row vector: the path to a .fmu archive or to an already-extracted FMU directory.

option pairs: 'Name' (block label / library title, default the FMU model identifier), 'IconDir' (directory to extract the FMU icon into), 'LibraryFile' (also write a one-block library.json to this path), 'LibraryId' (the library id, default user.<name>).

param_output_item.param_description: a structure describing the generated block, in the same schema as a library.json block entry.

description.p: fmuToBlock is the nflow FMU import assistant. It reads an FMU's modelDescription.xml and produces a native-looking nflow block: one input port per variable with causality input, one output port per output, the FMU parameters, the FMU's icon (its model.png when present, otherwise a labelled fallback), and a default path parameter pointing at the .fmu.

The generated block targets the engine's fmu handler, so placing it yields a working FMU block that simulates through the existing FMI path -- there is no new runtime. The value is authoring: an FMU becomes a first-class, named, icon'd palette block instead of a generic browse box. This pairs with the Modelica bridge, whose modelicaToFmu produces FMUs that fmuToBlock can then wrap.
With the 'LibraryFile' option, a one-block library.json is also written, ready to load in the nflow editor. Many FMUs ship no icon; in that case the render is a clean labelled fallback.
